1300: from διά and τελέω; to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to persist:--continue.
1301: from διά and τηρέω; to watch thoroughly, i.e. (positively and transitively) to observe strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to avoid wholly:--keep.
1302: from διά and τίς; through what cause ?, i.e. why?:--wherefore, why.
1303: middle voice from διά and τίθημι; to put apart, i.e. (figuratively) dispose (by assignment, compact, or bequest):--appoint, make, testator.
1304: from διά and the base of τρίβος; to wear through (time), i.e. remain:--abide, be, continue, tarry.
1305: from a compound of διά and τρέφω; nourishment:--food.
1306: from διά and αὐγάζω; to glimmer through, i.e. break (as day):--dawn.
1307: from διά and φαίνω; appearing through, i.e. "diaphanous":--transparent.
1308: from διά and φέρω; to bear through, i.e. (literally) transport; usually to bear apart, i.e. (objectively) to toss about (figuratively, report); subjectively, to "differ", or (by implication) surpass:--be better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent, make matter, publish, be of more value.
1309: from διά and φεύγω; to flee through, i.e. escape:--escape.
1310: from διά and a derivative of φήμη; to report thoroughly, i.e. divulgate:--blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame.
1311: from διαβάλλω and φθείρω; to rot thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to ruin (passively, decay utterly, figuratively, pervert):--corrupt, destroy, perish.
1313: from διαφέρω; varying; also surpassing:--differing, divers, more excellent.
1314: from διά and φυλάσσω; to guard thoroughly, i.e. protect:--keep.
1315: from διά and a derivative of χείρ; to handle thoroughly, i.e. lay violent hands upon:--kill, slay.
1316: from διά and the middle voice of χωρίζω; to remove (oneself) wholly, i.e. retire:--depart.
1318: from διδάσκω; (subjectively) instructed, or (objectively) communicated by teaching:--taught, which … teacheth.
1319: from διδάσκαλος; instruction (the function or the information):--doctrine, learning, teaching.
1320: from διδάσκω; an instructor (genitive case or specially):--doctor, master, teacher.
1321: a prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb (to learn); to teach (in the same broad application):--teach.
1322: from διδάσκω; instruction (the act or the matter):--doctrine, hath been taught.
1323: from δίς and δραχμή; a double drachma (didrachm):--tribute.
1324: prolongation from δίς; double, i.e. twin; Didymus, a Christian:--Didymus.
1325: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an alternative in most of the tenses); to give (used in a very wide application, properly, or by implication, literally or figuratively; greatly modified by the connection):--adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit, deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minister, number, offer, have power, put, receive, set, shew, smite (+ with the hand), strike (+ with the palm of the hand), suffer, take, utter, yield.
1326: from διά and ἐγείρω; to wake fully; i.e. arouse (literally or figuratively):--arise, awake, raise, stir up.
1327: from διά and ἔξοδος; an outlet through, i.e. probably an open square (from which roads diverge):--highway.
1329: from διά and ἑρμηνεύω; to explain thoroughly, by implication, to translate:--expound, interpret(-ation).
1330: from διά and ἔρχομαι; to traverse (literally):--come, depart, go (about, abroad, everywhere, over, through, throughout), pass (by, over, through, throughout), pierce through, travel, walk through.
1331: from διά and ἐρωτάω; to question throughout, i.e. ascertain by interrogation:--make enquiry for.
1332: from δίς and ἔτος; of two years (in age):--two years old.
1333: from διετής; a space of two years (biennium):--two years.
1334: from διά and ἡγέομαι; to relate fully:--declare, shew, tell.
1336: neuter of a compound of διά and a derivative of an alternate of φέρω; carried through, i.e. (adverbially with εἰς and ὁ prefixed) perpetually:--+ continually, for ever.
1337: from δίς and θάλασσα; having two seas, i.e. a sound with a double outlet:--where two seas meet.
1338: from διά and the base of ἱκανός; to reach through, i.e. penetrate:--pierce.
1339: from διά and ἵστημι; to stand apart, i.e. (reflexively) to remove, intervene:--go further, be parted, after the space of.
1340: from διά and a derivative of ἰσχυρός; to stout it through, i.e. asservate:--confidently (constantly) affirm.
1341: from δίκαιος and κρίσις; a just sentence:--righteous judgment.
1342: from δίκη; equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent, holy (absolutely or relatively):--just, meet, right(-eous).
1343: from δίκαιος; equity (of character or act); specially (Christian) justification:--righteousness.
1344: from δίκαιος; to render (i.e. show or regard as) just or innocent:--free, justify(-ier), be righteous.
1345: from δικαιόω; an equitable deed; by implication, a statute or decision:--judgment, justification, ordinance, righteousness.
1348: from a derivative of δίκη; a judger:--judge.
1349: probably from δεικνύω; right (as self-evident), i.e. justice (the principle, a decision, or its execution):--judgment, punish, vengeance.
1350: probably from a primary verb (to cast); a seine (for fishing):--net.
1351: from δίς and λόγος; equivocal, i.e. telling a different story:--double-tongued.
1352: from διά and ὅς; through which thing, i.e. consequently:--for which cause, therefore, wherefore.
1353: from διά and ὁδεύω; to travel through:--go throughout, pass through.
1355: from διό and περ; on which very account:--wherefore.
1356: from the alternate of Ζεύς and the alternate of πίπτω; sky-fallen (i.e. an aerolite):--which fell down from Jupiter.
1357: from a compound of διά and a derivative of ὀρθός, meaning to straighten thoroughly; rectification, i.e. (specially) the Messianic restauration:--reformation.
1358: from διά and ὀρύσσω; to penetrate burglariously:--break through (up).
1359: from the alternate of Ζεύς and a form of the base of κοράσιον; sons of Jupiter, i.e. the twins Dioscuri:--Castor and Pollux.
1360: from διά and ὅτι; on the very account that, or inasmuch as:--because (that), for, therefore.
1361: from the alternate of Ζεύς and τρέφω; Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity:--Diotrephes.
1362: from δίς and (probably) the base of πλείων; two-fold:--double, two-fold more.
1365: from δίς; properly, to duplicate, i.e. (mentally) to waver (in opinion):--doubt.
1366: from δίς and στόμα; double-edged:--with two edges, two-edged.
1367: from δίς and χίλιοι; two thousand:--two thousand.
1368: from διά and (to filter); to strain out:--strain at (probably by misprint).
1369: from a derivative of δίς; to make apart, i.e. sunder (figuratively, alienate):--set at variance.
1370: from a derivative of δίς and στάσις; disunion, i.e. (figuratively) dissension:--division, sedition.
1371: from a compound of a derivative of δίς and a derivative of (to cut); to bisect, i.e. (by extension) to flog severely:--cut asunder (in sunder).
1372: from a variation of δίψος; to thirst for (literally or figuratively):--(be, be a-)thirst(-y).
1374: from δίς and ψυχή; two-spirited, i.e. vacillating (in opinion or purpose):--double minded.
1377: a prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb (to flee; compare the base of δειλός and διάκονος); to pursue (literally or figuratively); by implication, to persecute:--ensue, follow (after), given to, (suffer) persecute(-ion), press forward.
1378: from the base of δοκέω; a law (civil, ceremonial or ecclesiastical):--decree, ordinance.
1379: from δόγμα; to prescribe by statute, i.e. (reflexively) to submit to, ceremonially rule:--be subject to ordinances.
1380: a prolonged form of a primary verb, (used only in an alternate in certain tenses; compare the base of δεικνύω) of the same meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or uncertainly):--be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow.
1381: from δόκιμος; to test (literally or figuratively); by implication, to approve:--allow, discern, examine, X like, (ap-)prove, try.
1382: from the same as δόκιμος; test (abstractly or concretely); by implication, trustiness:--experience(-riment), proof, trial.
1383: neuter of a presumed derivative of δοκιμή; a testing; by implication, trustworthiness:--trial, trying.
1384: from δοκέω; properly, acceptable (current after assayal), i.e. approved:--approved, tried.
1385: from δέχομαι (through the idea of holding up); a stick of timber:--beam.
1387: from δόλιος; to be guileful:--use deceit.
1388: from an obsolete primary verb, (probably meaning to decoy; compare δελεάζω); a trick (bait), i.e. (figuratively) wile:--craft, deceit, guile, subtilty.
1389: from δόλος; to ensnare, i.e. (figuratively) adulterate:--handle deceitfully.
1390: from the base of δίδωμι; a present:--gift.
1391: from the base of δοκέω; glory (as very apparent), in a wide application (literal or figurative, objective or subjective):--dignity, glory(-ious), honour, praise, worship.
1392: from δόξα; to render (or esteem) glorious (in a wide application):--(make) glorify(-ious), full of (have) glory, honour, magnify.
1394: from the base of δίδωμι; a giving; by implication, (concretely) a gift:--gift, giving.
1395: from the base of δίδωμι; a giver:--giver.
1396: from a presumed compound of δοῦλος and ἄγω; to be a slave-driver, i.e. to enslave (figuratively, subdue):--bring into subjection.
1398: from δοῦλος; to be a slave to (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary):--be in bondage, (do) serve(-ice).
1399: feminine of δοῦλος; a female slave (involuntarily or voluntarily):--handmaid(-en).
